title: Reading Section C 仔细阅读 2
paperTitle: 大学英语四级标准模拟卷 05
passage:
In many cities, the people who live closest together know least about each other. A recent experiment in three neighbourhoods tried to change that with a very old idea: a list of what neighbours can offer one another.

The project began with a simple questionnaire delivered to eight hundred homes. Residents were asked to write down one skill they would be willing to share, such as repairing a bicycle or filling in a form, and one thing they needed help with. The replies were surprising in two ways. Only about a fifth of the forms came back, yet those who replied offered far more than the organisers had expected. More importantly, the most frequent request was not practical at all: many people asked for company, someone to walk with in the evenings, or a neighbour willing to knock on the door once a week.

The organisers resisted the temptation to build an app. They printed a small booklet instead and asked the manager of the local shop to keep copies behind the counter. Older residents told them that a screen was exactly the thing that had made them feel excluded. A booklet, by contrast, could be read at the bus stop and passed on to a friend.

Two years later the project survives in a modest form: a monthly repair afternoon, a walking group on Tuesdays, and a list of people who will lend a ladder or a drill. The organisers measure success not by the number of services exchanged but by how quickly newcomers are noticed. 'In a good network,' one of them says, 'a new family is invited to something within a month, without anyone being officially asked to do it.'

questions.q: What surprised the organisers about the replies to the questionnaire?
options: Almost every household returned a form.
Very few residents offered any skills.
The most common request was for company.
Residents asked for an app instead of a booklet.
questions.explain: 第二段说 Only about a fifth of the forms came back，与 A 相反；但 the most frequent request was not practical at all: many people asked for company，故选 C。

questions.q: Why did the organisers print a booklet instead of building an app?
options: An app would have cost too much to develop.
The local shop offered to pay for the printing.
A booklet could be updated more easily.
Older residents said screens made them feel excluded.
questions.explain: 第三段说 Older residents told them that a screen was exactly the thing that had made them feel excluded，因此改印小册子，故选 D。

questions.q: How do the organisers judge whether the project is working?
options: By how quickly a new family is invited to something.
By the number of services exchanged each month.
By the number of booklets printed.
By how much money the project raises.
questions.explain: 最后一段说 The organisers measure success not by the number of services exchanged but by how quickly newcomers are noticed，并以 a new family is invited to something within a month 作具体说明，故选 A。
